title: OverSire events
description: One row of the events table (OVERSIRE-377). Each change in the work makes one row: agent sessions, turns, waits, your prompts and decisions, git, CI, provider activity, automation. The home daemon holds the full table. Each other daemon keeps a local copy and sends its rows to the home. The kinds are in event-kinds.json. Routes: POST /v1/events, POST /v1/events/links, GET /v1/items/{key}/events, GET /v1/events/rows. The live tail is the frame {type: event} on the WebSocket of the daemon. The SQL columns use snake_case (seen_at, parent_item, actor_type, on_behalf). Dates are ISO 8601 UTC.

Key.description: An item key in upper case, for example OVERSIRE-374.

Kind.description: domain.verb. An open set: the catalog is event-kinds.json. A reader keeps a row of a kind that it does not know.

ActorType.description: human: a person (the user, or a tracker member). agent: a coding agent. system: the daemon or the app on its own (queue, runbook, automation). provider: a vendor system (github-actions).

EventDraft.description: An Event before the home daemon gets it: no seq, no seenAt. The body of POST /v1/events.

id.description: <source>:<native id>, for example git:9d1e07a2:refs/heads/oversire-374 or gha:812:1:completed. A poll and a webhook of the same change give the same id. A repeat is a no-op.

at.description: When it happened. An outbox keeps this time.

item.description: Absent when no rule finds one.

parentItem.description: Set at write time when known. The item_links table corrects it later.

project.description: The tracker project, for example oversire.

machine.description: The machine where it happened, for example mini.

provider.description: The adapter of a provider row (plane, github). Absent for local sources.

session.description: The session key or id, for example work:OVERSIRE-374.

corr.description: Pairs rows: wait.started with wait.ended, turn.started with turn.ended.

actor.description: An email, harness/model (claude/opus-5-5), queue, runbook:<name>, github-actions.

onBehalf.description: The human who started it, for agent and system rows.

via.description: hook, git, app@<machine>, cli, poll, webhook, daemon.

summary.description: At most 200 code points. The only text that leaves the home daemon, and only when private is false.

payload.description: The fields of the kind (event-kinds.json). At most 4 KB. Kept 90 days on the home, never mirrored.

private.description: True for prompt text: the summary does not leave the user's Macs either. Absent means false.

Event.description: One row of the events table. An EventDraft plus seq and seenAt.

seq.description: The row number on the daemon that answers. Only a cursor: each daemon has its own.

seenAt.description: When the daemon that answers got it.

EventQuery.description: The query of GET /v1/items/{key}/events, as URL parameters. GET /v1/events/rows takes only after and limit.

tree.description: Also the rows where parentItem is the item.

after.description: A seq: only rows after it.

kinds.description: Only these kinds. A kind that ends with .* takes the whole domain (git.*).

EventPage.description: The answer of GET /v1/items/{key}/events. Rows in seq order.

next.description: The after value of the next page.

head.description: The last seq of the daemon.

EventAppendResult.description: The answer of POST /v1/events. accepted counts the new rows; a repeat id is not new.

EventFrame.description: The WebSocket frame {type: event} of the daemon: one new row. The home daemon sends each row; another daemon sends its own rows.

parent.description: Absent: the item has no parent now.

ItemLinks.description: The body of POST /v1/events/links. The app sends the parent of each item after a tracker poll. The daemon sets parentItem on the old rows again.
